resolved_findings.title: Existing explicit Windows ACLs survive private-directory protection
resolved_findings.evidence: Prior reviewed snapshot: apps/control-api/src/identity/runtime.ts:29 removed inherited ACEs and replaced grants only for the current SID; lines 31-32 reset descendants to inherit from that parent. apps/control-api/src/server.ts:12 applies the helper to the PGlite data root. packages/store/src/owner-schema.ts:14 stores private session values in that database.
resolved_findings.breaking_input: An existing configured data directory with an explicit inheritable read grant for another local user/group, such as Everyone or Users.
resolved_findings.impact: The explicit grant remained on the data root and propagated to its database files, exposing private session values and other stored control data to another local principal. Raw session values alone are insufficient to forge a signed BetterAuth cookie; direct authentication bypass was not demonstrated.
resolved_findings.refutation: Removing inheritance does remove broad inherited grants, and a new directory usually has no extra explicit ACE. It does not remove an existing explicit grant for a different SID. A later protection of the nested owner key directory can protect identity.key, but it does not repair the separate database data root.
resolved_findings.suggestion: Replace the root DACL with a protected allowlist for the current owner before resetting descendants; verify the resulting root ACL and existing-directory behavior.
resolved_findings.validation: Original issue confirmed by source and documented icacls semantics. Final frozen-source remediation re-reviewed: runtime.ts:72 creates a fresh DirectorySecurity descriptor, lines 73-75 disable inheritance without copying ACEs and add only owner FullControl, and line 76 applies the DACL through .NET Framework Directory.SetAccessControl without changing the existing OS owner. The target is passed exclusively through a child environment variable; PSModulePath is constrained to the OS module directory. runtime.ts:20 resolves canonical aliases and compares Windows paths case-insensitively against shared roots. privateTree rejects linked descendants and escaping paths; lines 91-102 recheck each descendant and reset it individually with /L, without /T. No permissive root reset is introduced. Parent reports seven actual Windows OS/offline-CLI runtime tests green; this reviewer did not independently execute them. The earlier temporary ACL reproduction was rejected by automatic command review before execution and was not rerun.
